analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Nu Stadium on 1 or 2 December (Columbus list either date), only played if the series is 1-1, with kick-off still to be set; a draw goes to penalties. Columbus would travel south five days after hosting Game 2, and Miami's home record has been weaker than their away record this season according to MLSsoccer.com. This view will be rebuilt from the first two games.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals. A winner-take-all third game is usually tighter than the openers, and two coaches, Kily Gonzalez and Laurent Courtois, who have just faced each other twice will plan more carefully, so I lean slightly lower while still expecting goals from Messi and Suarez.

corners.text: The site expects 8.4 corners. As in the earlier games, Miami's central build-up produces few corners (two against Charlotte), so I lean a little lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. A third meeting in 11 days with elimination at stake should carry more fouls and bookings than the series opener; Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte, and Columbus had two players booked in their 4-3 win in Chicago.

shots.text: The site expects 27.3 shots. Both teams have been efficient rather than shot-heavy, and a decider should be more guarded, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target. I stay close to it: fewer shots in total, but Messi, Suarez, Tapia and Mendez all finish well, so the share on target should stay high.
